transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-05 10:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Priya Nadar (Aperture ML), Carlos Mendes (Aperture SRE), Leah Kim (Product)
Recorded at: 2026-08-05T10:00:00-07:00

Summary (auto): quick status on quality deltas from INT8/FP8 blends, root-cause discussion for the 2.4% SNR drop on customer NLU set, throughput tuning plan, and next steps for on-prem mini-run.

Topics: results recap, perf deltas, regression triage, batching/autobatching knobs, KV cache implications, rollout plan for canary on Dedicated, next steps and owners.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey team, thanks for joining. Quick check, audio ok?
[00:05] Priya (Aperture): yeah, good here, thanks Maya.
[00:10] Ethan (Redwood SE): audio good. I'll share the results sheet in the chat — link: https://redwood.app/s/precision-poc/results-aug5 (shared) 
[00:18] Leah (Aperture): got it, opening now.

[00:30] Maya: Agenda: 1) recap last week's runs, 2) deep-dive on the small quality regressions we saw with INT8 blend, 3) throughput/latency tuning, 4) plan to run a short on-prem smoke with your infra. Sound right?
[00:45] Carlos: yes, that's it.

[01:05] Ethan: ok quick recap — we ran two main sweep axes: precision blend (FP16 -> INT8 aggressive) and then an FP8 midline. We measured quality against the 1k prompt set Priya shared and also ran a 10k synthetic inference workload for perf. The high level: INT8 aggressive dropped SNR on the NLU set ~2.1–2.6% median depending on prompt length. FP8 seemed much closer to baseline, like 0.3–0.6% delta. Latency P50 improved ~18–28% for int8 in our env, P95 improvements were smaller because of stragglers.

[02:00] Priya: just to clarify, the 2.6% was on short prompts (<=64 tokens) right?
[02:05] Ethan: correct, shorter sequences saw larger quality deltas likely due to quant noise interacting with soft prompts, also the tokenizer edge-cases. For longer seqs it's closer.

[03:12] Priya: is that SNR computed per-example or macro-averaged? I noticed the sheet has both.
[03:18] Ethan: per-example, then averaged; we also included exact-match for your classification intents. There's a tab labeled "quality-summary" with both metrics. Sorry if the auto-naming is a bit messy.

[04:00] Maya: on the regression triage — can we walk through the examples where int8 flipped the label? Priya do you have one or two to highlight?
[04:12] Priya: yes, example ID 1223 and 1456. With INT8 the model changed intent from "cancel subscription" to "change subscription" — subtle but problematic.
[04:25] Ethan: I pulled logits for 1223. There's a small logits compression after quant that makes the top-2 margin smaller. We'll dump the kv-cache traces, though sometimes the transcripts show "KV cash" in logs, that was me, sorry.
[04:45] (small laughter)

[05:05] Carlos: from infra perspective, the P95 tails look like they correlate with batch spikes at 512 when concurrent streams hit the same worker. Are you doing continuous batching?
[05:15] Ethan: yes continuous batching + dynamic batching policy. The P95 tail is partly due to head-of-line blocking at high concurrency. We can tune batch windows, reduce max batch size and increase parallel worker count to flatten that tail.

[06:20] Leah: what's the best lever for you to nudge quality back while keeping most of the latency gains?
[06:28] Ethan: two levers: 1) hybrid precision where we keep attention matmul in FP16 and quantize only linear projection weights (the "precision blend" we talked about), or 2) selective dequant for top attention layers. Both mitigate quality loss; option 1 keeps >80% of latency gains, option 2 is safer but gives smaller latency improvements.

[07:10] Priya: so the hybrid approach — we saw earlier in the sheet a run called "int8-blend-80pct" that looked promising?
[07:18] Ethan: exactly. That run had an SNR delta of 0.8% but P50 still improved ~12%. It's a good compromise.

[07:50] Maya: quick note — we also tried a cache warmup trick where we pre-populate KV entries for known boilerplate prompts; that reduced cold-start penalties on short prompts and improved P95 by ~6%. Worth trying on your on-prem smoke.

[08:25] Carlos: for on-prem smoke, network egress from GPU nodes is a constraint. We'll only allow a small burst capacity. Do you have a low-IO mode?
[08:35] Ethan: yep, we can run a local-only inference mode with no external telemetry and reduced logging. That will lower egress. We'll document the exact flags. Maya will include those in the checklist.

[09:00] (00:09:00 timestamp)
[09:05] Priya: a question about eval thresholds — what would Redwood consider an acceptable SNR delta to approve canary rollout?
[09:12] Maya: typical guideline: for NLU we aim for <1% SNR delta and 0.5% for critical intents, but it's negotiable. For this POC, we agreed last week that Aperture's product team needs <1.5% overall on the 1k set and no high-severity intent flips.

[10:00] Priya: ok that matches internal goals.

[10:20] Ethan: small callout — we observed one regression cluster that looks tokenizer-specific. Some tokens get mapped differently under quant due to rounding in embedding matmul; might be an artifact in the conversion pipeline. We'll run a tokenization alignment pass and re-run the short prompts.

[11:05] Priya: can you share the raw logits and top-k lists? That helps our labelers triage.
[11:12] Ethan: yes adding to the sheet: logs tab -> raw-outputs.zip (will upload).

[12:00] Leah: on cost — curious what the estimated per-1M requests delta is for int8 vs fp16 on a dedicated node?
[12:08] Maya: ballpark, int8 can cut token compute cost roughly 35–45% depending on utilization; FP8 sits in the middle ~20–30%. We'll send a pricing delta in the quote. For your 99th-percentile workload, the savings footprint will be different; we'll model that in the next quote.

[13:00] Carlos: do you support encrypted KV caches/HSM for keys? We need KMS integration for on-prem keys.
[13:10] Ethan: yes we have KMS integrations and can support HSM-backed keys in Private. For the smoke we can demo with a customer-provided key stub.

[14:00] (speaker overlap, brief crosstalk)
[14:10] Priya: on the FP8 runs — they looked very close to baseline, any caveats?
[14:16] Ethan: FP8 is less aggressive and generally keeps numeric dynamic range better. Caveat: some hardware has limited optimized kernels for FP8 so latency wins may be smaller; but quality is usually better than int8. Also, quant conversion pipeline has a couple of micro losses on layernorm that we mitigate with small per-channel calibration.

[15:20] Maya: we ran a micro-ablation where we disabled prefix cache — quality unchanged but latency regressed. So caching is additive to both performance and quality stability (since cached prefixes avoid re-quantization noise).

[16:00] Priya: interesting — for our product many requests are short chat-like messages, so prefix caching could be a big win.

[16:25] Ethan: yes that aligns. We'll include a cache warm-up policy suggestion for your traffic shapes.

[17:10] Priya: about your automated rollback — if a canary exceeds our thresholds what happens?
[17:16] Maya: Redwood has automatic fallback policies. If quality delta over rolling window > threshold or error rate increases, we can fallback to FP16 model variant or previous pinned model version. It's configurable per-route. We'll share an example policy blob.

[18:08] Carlos: do you send us traces for auditing? We need audit logs for every model decision for compliance.
[18:15] Ethan: yes audit logs available in Console, with token-level usage, model version, rollout id. In Private we can stream to your SIEM.

[19:00] Maya: ok let's dive into the triage of the two problematic examples. Ethan, can you read the raw outputs?
[19:10] Ethan: for 1223 top-3 tokens pre-quant were: [cancel, stop, unsubscribe] with margins 0.42/0.18; post-int8 margins became 0.30/0.28 so top-1 not as dominant. That allowed the reranker to flip label in one variant. I'm attaching the delta plots in the sheet.

[20:05] Priya: interesting that reranker sensitivity amplifies small logits changes. Our reranker threshold is pretty fine-grained. Maybe we should relax for canary.

[21:00] Leah: would a small reranker threshold change be acceptable as a temporary canary mitigation?
[21:05] Maya: yes for canary we can relax reranker sensitivity or apply a soft-threshold only on canary traffic. But long-term we'd prefer kernel-level fixes.

[22:10] Ethan: one more approach: per-layer calibration tables — we could apply an additive correction to logits using a small bias vector calibrated on your set. That tends to remove systematic shifts. It's more engineering but stable.

[23:05] Priya: do you have an estimate how long calibration takes?
[23:10] Ethan: a calibration pass on 1k prompts takes about 20 minutes on a single GPU, producing correction vectors. We'll automate that in the next run.

[24:00] (mid-point check)
[24:12] Maya: timeline check: next week we aim to finish the int8/FP8 calibrated sweep and then run on-prem smoke. Any blockers?
[24:20] Carlos: need the low-IO flags and the install checklist.

[25:05] Maya: noted — I'll send those.

[25:30] Ethan: on the perf side, we noticed two hotspots: 1) head-of-line blocking at large batch windows, and 2) slow atomics in some older GPU drivers that worsen P95. For the latter we suggested specific nv driver versions in the sheet.

[26:10] Carlos: we run a slightly older driver on our infra for stability; can you list the exact versions that show the P95 improvement?

[26:18] Ethan: yes — we saw best numbers on 535.x drivers; older 520.x had worse tail behavior. We'll put exact bench numbers in the notes tab.

[27:00] Priya: about the 1k prompt set, we discovered a tokenization mismatch in our preprocessor — some leading whitespace caused different token boundaries. Could that explain part of the regressions?
[27:10] Ethan: absolutely, tokenization mismatch can amplify quant noise. If possible, run tokenizer alignment (we have a script) before the next sweep. I'll attach it.

[28:30] Leah: we need an explicit success criteria doc for the canary — what exact metrics and thresholds we'll watch.
[28:38] Maya: we'll create a one-pager: SNR delta, intent-flip count (high-sev), P95 latency delta, error rate. I'll draft and share by 2026-08-06.

[29:15] Priya: can you also include an experimental tag in outputs so we can filter canary traffic in our logs?
[29:20] Ethan: yes route-level metadata can include "redwood.canary=true" and a rollout id.

[30:00] (half hour mark)
[30:05] Carlos: small ask — can you produce a cost model for Dedicated nodes vs Hosted int8 runs comparing our current 2k requests/min baseline?
[30:14] Maya: we'll produce a model table; need your 95th-percentile concurrency and avg tokens per request (Priya?).

[30:20] Priya: average tokens ~64, 95th concurrency ~45.

[31:05] Ethan: with those numbers our initial model shows int8 on Dedicated with two 8-GPU nodes gives about 38% compute cost saving vs FP16 Hosted for your volume, but networking and ops overhead on-prem reduce some of that. We'll put numbers in the quote.

[32:00] Leah: about observability — do you export per-prompt embeddings and similarity hashes? For debugging we sometimes want to diff embeddings pre- and post-quant.

[32:08] Ethan: we can export embeddings but heavy egress; for the smoke we'll do local dumps. Production you'd stream to your analytics bucket.

[33:15] Priya: any known gotchas around beamsearch vs sampling with quant? We use top-k sampling.

[33:22] Ethan: top-k is generally more sensitive to small logit shifts; nucleus sampling can be slightly more robust. We can try both in AB tests.

[34:05] Maya: ok quick technical action: Ethan will run the calibration + int8-blend-80pct + fp8 sweep with tokenization alignment and upload logs. Priya to validate on label set.

[34:20] Ethan: noted. I'll start jobs after this call.

[35:00] (some typing/listening noise)
[35:40] Carlos: curious about the fallback delta time — if a canary fails, how fast can you revert?
[35:46] Maya: automatic rollback can be near-instant (within seconds) if triggered by health checks; full traffic re-routing depends on your routing gates but typically <5 minutes to flip to pinned variant.

[36:30] Priya: about data retention for this POC — how long will you keep logs?
[36:36] Maya: defaults to 30 days in hosted; for Private we can configure retention. We'll align on what you need for audit.

[37:20] Ethan: one more technical note — when we measured P95 improvements, the wall-clock improvements were larger on NVIDIA AXXX than older V100-series; hardware matters for int8 kernels. We'll call out recommended instance types.

[38:10] Leah: good — please call out hardware and driver combos in the docs.

[39:00] Priya: any blocker on our side to start the on-prem smoke next Thursday? We need the installer flags and the sample workload.

[39:10] Carlos: I can provision a small cluster.

[39:20] Maya: outstanding items: docs + checklist + quote from me, calibration and logs from Ethan, prompt set from Priya.

[40:00] (quiet for few seconds)
[40:12] Priya: quick FYI — our compliance team asked for SOC2 docs and a network diagram.
[40:18] Maya: sending SOC2 summary and I'll attach a sample network diagram. That's on my deliverables.

[41:05] Ethan: putting a note in the sheet — run-id PREC-0826-int8-blend-1 queued, ETA ~3 hours. I'll ping when done.

[42:00] Leah: great. Also want a short readout doc for our execs summarizing risk/benefit.

[42:08] Maya: we'll prepare a 1-page exec readout and include the cost table.

[43:00] Priya: question — are there any previous customers who ran similar precision blends and saw long-term drift?
[43:08] Ethan: a few; the long-term issues tended to be from model fine-tuning mismatch rather than quantization itself. We'll share anonymized postmortems.

[44:20] Carlos: about monitoring — will Redwood emit per-model health metrics to our Prometheus?
[44:26] Ethan: yes metrics endpoint + Grafana template for dashboards.

[45:05] Maya: ok let's do a short recap and decisions.

Recap:
- Run: Ethan to execute calibrated int8 + fp8 sweeps with tokenization alignment (Ethan)
- Data: Priya to send final 1k prompt set and baseline samples (Priya)
- Infra: Carlos to provision cluster and confirm driver version constraints (Carlos)
- Docs & Quote: Maya to send security checklist, low-IO flags, and updated quote with Dedicated sizing (Maya)

[46:30] Action owners + due dates repeated (see action_items).

[47:10] (brief side conversation about scheduling)
[48:00] Maya: final questions?
[48:05] Priya: none from me.
[48:10] Carlos: all good.
[48:15] Leah: thanks everyone.

[48:30] Maya: thanks — we'll follow up in the sheet and Slack. Next sync tentatively 2026-08-12 same time to review sweep results.

[49:00] (meeting end)

Artifacts shared: results spreadsheet (link above), raw-outputs.zip (will upload), installer flags doc (TODO), SOC2 summary (Maya to attach).
